rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Rutherford Scattering Experiment:** Alpha particles were fired at a thin gold foil. Most passed through with little deflection, but a few scattered at large angles (>90°). This disproved the Thomson plum-pudding model and established the nuclear model: a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus containing most of the atom's mass.  ·  **Nuclear Size vs Atom Size:** The nucleus is ~10⁻¹⁵ m (1-10 fm) while the atom is ~10⁻¹⁰ m (1 Å). The nucleus occupies ~10⁻¹⁵ of the atomic volume but contains >99.9% of the mass. The rest is empty space where electrons orbit.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not claim the experiment established a modern planetary electron orbit.  ·  Closest-approach estimates assume Coulomb interaction and head-on motion.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: For ²³⁵₉₂U, N=235−92=143.  ·  The nuclear radius scale is roughly 10⁵ times smaller than atomic radius.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Rutherford's foil experiment showed that the atom is mostly empty. Nearly every alpha particle went straight on, and a small number were turned through large angles. That is possible only if the positive charge and most of the mass sit in a nucleus far smaller than the atom.  ·  The working relations are Most alpha particles go almost straight through the foil and A few bounce back from a tiny positive nucleus. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Large-angle deflections imply → B  ·  The nuclear volume is smaller than the atomic volume by about → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Rutherford, Geiger and Marsden directed alpha particles at thin gold foil. Most passed almost straight through; a small fraction deflected sharply and very few returned. These observations could not be explained by positive charge spread uniformly through the atom.  ·  Rutherford inferred a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus containing nearly all atomic mass, surrounded by electrons; most atomic volume is empty space. Nuclear radius is about 10⁻¹⁵ m versus atomic radius about 10⁻¹⁰ m.  ·  For a head-on alpha particle, its kinetic energy converts to electrostatic potential energy at closest approach: Eα=(1/4πε₀)(2Ze²/rmin). Thus rmin=(1/4πε₀)(2Ze²/Eα), under the Coulomb-scattering model.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Worked case  ·  **Nuclear Density:** Nearly constant for all nuclei: ρ = mass/volume ≈ A·1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg / (4/3 π (1.2×10⁻¹⁵ A¹ᐟ³)³) ≈ 2.3×10¹⁷ kg/m³. This constancy supports the liquid-drop model and the idea that nucleons are closely packed.  ·  A vector answer needs a direction as well as a magnitude.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A special case, such as a right angle or a steady temperature, has to be stated before it is used.  ·  An atom is about 10^−10 m across and a nucleus is about 10^−15 m across. Find the ratio of the nuclear volume to the atomic volume.  ·  Nuclear notation ᴬ_ZX gives proton number Z, nucleon number A and neutron number N=A−Z. Isotopes share Z but have different A; isobars share A but have different Z.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Example: uranium-235 has Z=92, A=235 and N=143. Its nuclear charge is +92e.
